data.context: 05.13.19 Threat Report < https://www.deepwatch.com/blog_category/threat-report/> Profile of an Adversary - FIN7 By Bryan Austin Estimated Reading Time: 10 minutes The majority of companies in either the Retail or Hospitality industries are [sadly] familiar with FIN7.

evidence.quote: The majority of companies in either the Retail or Hospitality industries are [sadly] familiar with FIN7.

data.context: Since then FIN7 has been identified by many organizations, including: FireEye - FIN7 CrowdStrike - Carbon Spider Media - Carbanak Gang/Group

evidence.quote: FIN7 CrowdStrike - Carbon Spider

data.context: This group has suspected ties to Russian organized crime and has netted roughly $1 Billion USD in the last half-decade.

object.name: suspected ties to Russian organized crime

evidence.quote: has suspected ties to Russian organized crime

data.context: Additionally, the group has strong ties to Ukraine, where 3 members of the FIN7 group were arrested in 2018, though often times Russian cyber operations find their first deployment in Ukraine.

evidence.quote: Additionally, the group has strong ties to Ukraine, where 3 members of the FIN7 group were arrested in 2018,

data.context: Targeting The FIN7 group began by targeting banks in the Russian Federation, but in 2015 began to transition their targeting to a broader scope to include the Middle East, Europe and the United States.

evidence.quote: Targeting The FIN7 group began by targeting banks in the Russian Federation

data.context: Historically the group has targeted individuals who are listed in the organizations SEC

evidence.quote: Historically the group has targeted individuals

data.context: This starts as a spear phishing email sent to the initial target.

evidence.quote: sent to the initial target

data.context: The exchange then leads to an initial document delivery that is usually benign but possesses a tracking pixel that allows the actor to verify whether or not the target is opening attachments, and if so can provide initial visibility into the system of the target.

evidence.quote: allows the actor to verify whether or not the target is opening attachments

data.context: This document has either a VBA macro or an embedded OLE which persuades the target to run these in order to drop the first stage loaders.

evidence.quote: This document has either a VBA macro or an embedded OLE

data.context: If the first stage loader is not dropped, the attacker resumes the threat tactic and escalates the issue to the target's supervisor which indicates an extensive amount of OSINT and revealing the extent the

evidence.quote: which indicates an extensive amount of OSINT

data.context: There is also a possible connection to the 2016 SWIFT attacks, many of which have since been attributed to North Korea, however evidence of this is limited and open to interpretation.

evidence.quote: There is also a possible connection to the 2016 SWIFT attacks,

data.context: The group typically follows a standard sequence of events: Spear phishing a target with a document loaded with a malware payload which as of May 2018 has been the Gri " on payload, or a combination of SQLRat and DNSBot historically.

evidence.quote: Spear phishing a target with a document loaded with a malware payload

data.context: This begins the beaconing back to the Cobalt Strike servers.

evidence.quote: beaconing back to the Cobalt Strike servers

data.context: From there the adversary loads process injection tools or memory scrapers (commonly mimikatz) and pivots using tools like powersploit, RDP services, and PowerAdmin Exec.

object.name: process injection tools or memory scrapers (commonly mimikatz)

evidence.quote: loads process injection tools or memory scrapers (commonly mimikatz)

evidence.quote: heavily targets the following CVEs: CVE-2015-2545

data.context: The group has begun branching out in using various malware versions and a full listing of the known IOCs for the new SQLRat and DNSBot additionally the Astra PHP panel are included at the end of this document as well as a list of links to the open source projects to allow for greater research.

evidence.quote: a full listing of the known IOCs for the new SQLRat and DNSBot additionally the Astra PHP panel are included

data.context: Due to FIN7's heavy use of spear phishing to deliver malicious MSFT O # ce documents to users, the most common exploits are scripts written in PowerShell or VBA and executed as macros in the documents.

evidence.quote: Due to FIN7's heavy use of spear phishing

data.context: Though FIN7 does not actively exploit vulnerabilities at the time of this writing (e.g. CVE's 2545, 1701, & 0199), they can potentially begin to do so in the future.
Vulnerability Management allows you to take an in depth stock of your IT assets.
